source: The three shapes US federal student-loan repayment takes — a level payment over a fixed term, a share of discretionary income with the remainder forgiven after a horizon, and the level plan with extra on top — stated as shapes, not as any year's rules, plan names, or poverty table.
confidenceNote: Every figure here is the round number the shape is usually described with, not a current regulation: a 10-year standard term, 10% of discretionary income, discretionary income above 150% of a poverty line rounded to $15,000 for one person, forgiveness after 20 years (25 for graduate borrowings). Servicers, plan names and thresholds change; the person's own plan letter wins over all of it.
note: Read by engines/studentloans.js (the Student Loan Decision room, D-101). The standard plan uses the loan's listed minimum when there is one and the level payment over standardTermYears at the loan's rate when there is not. The income-driven payment is max(0, (gross − discretionaryPovertyMultiple × povertyLineDollars) × idrShareOfDiscretionary ÷ 12), held flat because income growth is not modelled. The aggressive plan is the standard plan plus household.studentLoans.extraMonthlyCents. A forgiven balance may be taxed as income in the year it is forgiven; that tax is named, not modelled.
povertyLineNote: A household of one, rounded. A convention for the shape of the calculation, not the current federal poverty guideline for any year or household size.
forgivenessNote: The room proposes forgivenessYears; a person who borrowed for graduate study types 25. Forgiveness of 0 or blank means the income-driven payment runs until the loans clear, with no write-off.

aggressive.note: The standard plan's payments plus a fixed extra every month, applied through engines/debt.js the way Debt Payoff applies an extra. With no extra typed it equals the standard plan.

interestDeduction.note: The federal student loan interest deduction (D-247): above the line, up to the cap a year across all student loans, phased out linearly over the income band for the filing status; not allowed filing separately. Recalled 2024 figures, to verify against the current IRS table. Applied per loan here, so two large loans can together overstate the cap.
